children: Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem has hinted that interest rates are likely to rise at the central bank’s year-end meeting on Dec. 9.
In a speech to the Economic Club of Canada in Toronto, Macklem downplayed the positive effects of declining energy prices and said that inflation remains an issue.

“So far, businesses have largely absorbed the higher production and transport costs. But historical lags and our own business surveys suggest more pass-through to consumer prices in the year ahead,” said the central bank governor.
Avery Shenfeld, chief economist at CIBC bank (CM) wrote in a note to clients after the speech that Macklem was downplaying the disinflationary impact of falling oil prices.
The economist added that the governor’s focus on inflation risks suggests the central bank plans to deliver a second consecutive interest rate hike in December.
“There was no direct reference to the December meeting, but what was apparent was that the governor was going out of his way to not show any changes in his thinking,” wrote Shenfeld.
Financial markets are currently pricing in a 79% chance of a 25-basis point rate hike from the Bank of Canada on Dec. 9, according to data from LSEG (LSEG).
Those odds are up from 63% a week ago. Notably, all of Canada’s big six banks expect the Bank of Canada to raise borrowing costs in December.
The Bank of Canada last raised its key interest rate on Oct. 28, increasing its benchmark overnight rate by 25 basis points to 2.50%.

title: Bank Of Canada Governor Hints At December Rate Hike
